newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia's Anwar says ringgit returning to normal.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's Anwar says ringgit returning to normal.

text.p: Acting Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Tuesday that the beleagured ringgit is already returning to normal.
"I believe it (the ringgit) is returning (to normalcy) already," Anwar said, when asked when the ringgit would reverse its declining trend.
"I don't think we are for continued rise in interest rates, or a strong interest rate regime," he added to reporters following a speech at an Islamic capital markets conference.
He said the recent rise in interest rates was due to events in the foreign exchange market where the ringgit has been under selling pressure from speculators.
Anwar said in a speech earlier that "we are confident that once the speculative activity subsides, the trend for the ringgit will reverse to reflect the underlying favourable fundamentals."
Asked if the Malaysia will revise down its growth projections, Anwar said, "It depends on how long interest rates remain high."
"I do not think we will risk the ringgit, the market or the growth. That is why we will have to monitor this closely and make the necessary adjustments," he said.
But, he said there was no fear of the Malaysian economy overheating. He said the projections being made by the market highlighted only a few mega-projects.
"These are to my mind irresponsible projections and estimates, because it would actually portray a different view of the path of development the country is taking," Anwar said.

"It is true some projects are critical, ... but it is not in the manner that people are projecting. That is why I am not too unduly worried about what is being said about overheating," the acting prime minister said.
"Finally, we have got to look at the figures. And we are extremely cautious and mindful that we do not repeat the excesses and mistakes by other countries," he said.

Earlier on Tuesday, the ringgit slipped to a 33-month low of 2.5700 against the dollar as funds sold the Malaysian currency following Anwar's comment on Monday that the ringgit is within a reasonable range.
However, the ringgit recovered on Tuesday morning as funds started to take profits.
At 0400 GMT, the ringgit was trading at 2.5540/80 to a dollar.
